inputs.cite: jg1@01:03-01:46 (Duffy's values as Ghijselen reads them; M-711)

day.reading: G_f = T_obs / n_obs is a throughput that already counts overlapping fixations (G1 q1; ¶7)
day.holds: 35,000 years is the mean spacing g G_f, not one allele's time; the marathon's analogue of G_f is the 0.24 s per finisher at the line, not 4 h per runner, so T/G_f counts right at any overlap (M-706); the comment's '4 times' reproduces under neither reading (1e4 or 2.74)

critic.reading: the 180 is a serial count: one allele per 35,000 years (the book's Appendix A, G2g q1)
critic.holds: on that reading the marathon is exact: n t = 240,000 h against 4 h in parallel, a factor of n; the concurrent-completion reading makes the time grow as ln k (2.74x from 200 to 2e6), not as k

notes: Exact on rationals for the marathon bound; floats elsewhere. The 0.24 s line time is a constructed bound (all runners in one 4 h window), not a race statistic; with a longer finish window the line time grows and the concurrency falls, the identity is unchanged. The H_k ratio models each duration as Exp(1); it is one charitable reading of the comment, not a population-genetics model, and it needs all k changes present at once.
